subject: point transect: radial v's perpendicular distances

messages.author: 0e6482c73c7cede4
messages.subject: point transect: radial v's perpendicular distances
parts:
Dear Distance-sampling list,

I have avian point transect data that was collected using perpendicular
distance categories. From what I have read from the 1993 edition of Intro.
to Distance Sampling, it appears that only radial distances are used for
point transects, whereas line transects can use either radial or
perpendicular distances. Can perpendicular distance categories be used for
analyzing point transect data in DISTANCE?

Thanks,
Mike Baldwin
graduate student
mba...@lsu.edu

messages.author: d718c6bb1db28db2
messages.subject: Re: point transect: radial v's perpendicular distances
parts:
> > I have avian point transect data that was collected using perpendicular
> > distance categories. From what I have read from the 1993 edition of Intro.
> > to Distance Sampling, it appears that only radial distances are used for
> > point transects, whereas line transects can use either radial or
> > perpendicular distances. Can perpendicular distance categories be used for
> > analyzing point transect data in DISTANCE?

For point transects, there is only one detection distance. For line
transects, you can have either the distance of the detected animal from
the observer (the radial distance) or its shortest distance to the line
(the perpendicular distance). For points, distance to the observer and
distance to the point are the same thing. This distance is termed the
radial distance.

Steve Buckland
